content: Imagine a world where everyone looked exactly the same, had the same name, and liked the same things. How would your mom know who you are when it's time for dinner? It's a real-world mystery!
What makes you different from the person sitting next to you? If you couldn't show them your face, how would you describe who you are?

content.title: The Magic Fingerprint
content.description: Look at this fingerprint! Every single person in the world has a different pattern on their fingers. It's like a secret code built right into your hand.

content: All the things that make you special—your name, your age, your favorite color, and even your fingerprint—make up your Identity. When you say 'About Me', you are sharing your identity with the world!

question: Which of the following is a part of your personal identity?
options: The color of the sky outside
Your own name and your age

content: Pause here. Ask the child to say their full name loudly and proudly. Have them hold up fingers to show their age.
Reflection Time: Think about your best friend. What are two things they like to do that are different from what you like? Does being different make it fun to play together?
Sometimes kids think they have to like the same things as their friends. It's perfectly okay to have your own favorite games and foods!
Just like you have your own identity, everything in nature has an identity too! Animals have different names and shapes. Even trees have different types of leaves so we can tell them apart.
Mastery Challenge: Create your own 'About Me' badge! Take a piece of paper, write your name in big letters, draw a picture of your face, and color it with your favorite colors. Wear it proudly!
